harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 as a router with routed IPv4 addresses on both its transit segments (eth1: 172.20.1.1/24 toward node2, eth2: 172.20.2.1/24 toward node3), enabled IPv4 forwarding, and gave node2/node3 addresses+routes on their ens7 links so they reach each other through node1. Made the configuration self-restoring across reboot: node1 uses a new systemd unit ([REDACTED].service) because SONiC's networking.service only auto-brings-up eth0, ignoring interfaces.d for eth1/eth2; node2 and node3 use standard /etc/network/interfaces.d/ens7.cfg static configs (natively reconciled by ifupdown at boot). Verified via two independent node1 reboots and one reboot each of node2/node3 that boot_id changed each time and node2<->node3 connectivity (bidirectional ping) came back with zero manual intervention.
actions_performed: Mapped topology: node1 eth1<->node2 ens7, node1 eth2<->node3 ens7 (confirmed via link-local ipv6 ping on each interface)
Assigned node1 eth1=172.20.1.1/24, eth2=172.20.2.1/24 via /etc/network/interfaces.d/eth1 and eth2
Enabled net.ipv4.ip_forward and per-interface forwarding on node1 via /etc/sysctl.d/99-antrieb.conf
Assigned node2 ens7=172.20.1.2/24 with route to 172.20.2.0/24 via node1, via /etc/network/interfaces.d/ens7.cfg
Assigned node3 ens7=172.20.2.2/24 with route to 172.20.1.0/24 via node1, via /etc/network/interfaces.d/ens7.cfg
Verified node2<->node3 ping worked through node1 before any restart
Captured pre-restart boot_id baselines for node1, node2, node3
Rebooted node1; found eth1/eth2 addressing did NOT return automatically (SONiC networking.service only manages eth0)
Root-caused via journalctl -u networking.service that ifupdown2's boot sequence never called ifup on eth1/eth2
Created and enabled /etc/systemd/system/[REDACTED].service (oneshot, WantedBy=multi-user.target) to ifup eth1 and eth2 after networking.service
Applied fix live and verified connectivity restored

Rebooted node1 a second time to prove the new systemd unit self-applies at boot without manual steps; confirmed new boot_id, addressing, forwarding sysctls, and node2<->node3 connectivity all recovered automatically
Restarted node2: captured baseline boot_id, rebooted, confirmed new boot_id, verified ens7 addressing/route restored automatically, verified ping to node3
Restarted node3: captured baseline boot_id, rebooted, confirmed new boot_id, verified ens7 addressing/route restored automatically, verified ping to node2

evidence.requirement: node1 has routed addresses on both segments (eth1, eth2) and forwarding enabled
evidence.summary: eth1=172.20.1.1/24 and eth2=172.20.2.1/24 assigned; ip_forward and per-interface forwarding=1 confirmed live and again after second reboot

evidence.requirement: Working path between node2 and node3 through node1 (pre-restart)
evidence.summary: node2 (172.20.1.2) and node3 (172.20.2.2) configured with routes via node1; bidirectional ping succeeded with 0% loss before any restart
boot_id e5a08f0f-... and live eth1/eth2 addressing captured pre-restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart #1 acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: reboot command acknowledged and returned before disconnect; subsequent connection reset/timeout proved the node went down; boot_id changed to 7136a83f-... on return

evidence.requirement: node1 restart #1 recovery gap discovered and fixed, then proven persistent via a second independent restart
evidence.summary: After reboot #1, eth1/eth2 had no IPv4 (SONiC networking.service only manages eth0); created/enabled [REDACTED].service, verified live fix, then rebooted node1 a second time; boot_id changed again (5a94696d-...) and eth1/eth2 addressing, forwarding sysctls, and node2<->node3 ping all recovered with zero manual steps
boot_id 2ba78175-... and ens7 172.20.1.2/24 with route to 172.20.2.0/24 captured pre-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
evidence.summary: sudo reboot acknowledged before disconnect; boot_id changed to 68060384-...; ens7 address/route restored automatically via interfaces.d/ens7.cfg; ping to node3 succeeded post-restart
boot_id f6f9440e-... and ens7 172.20.2.2/24 with route to 172.20.1.0/24 captured pre-restart

evidence.requirement: node3 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
evidence.summary: sudo reboot acknowledged before disconnect; boot_id changed to 9c9887c6-...; ens7 address/route restored automatically; bidirectional ping between node2 and node3 succeeded post-restart
